newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank upgrades Bekaert EPS rating.
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank upgrades Bekaert EPS rating.

text.p: Belgium's Generale Bank said on Tuesday it would revise upwards its 1996 earnings per share forecast for steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, while maintaining its hold recommendation on the share.
"We prefer to wait for more evidence of the European activities to pick up before upgrading our current hold recommendation," Generale Bank said in an equity report following a company visit.

"As only two-thirds of the 1996 restructuring cost will be booked under the group's operational results, we increase our 1996 EPS estimate to 270 Belgian francs from 50 francs (against 1,323 francs during 1995)," Generale Bank said.
Earnings per share for 1997 was forecast at 1,020 francs.

The report said Bekaert estimated 1997 to be a transitional year, expecting after-tax profit from recurrent activities at around 2.25 billion Belgian francs or still 30 percent below the 1995 profit level.
Bekaert was not available for comment on the report.
The bank said it was considering whether to lower their full-year 1996 dividend forecast.

"This implies a P/E of 19, which is not excessive," the report said, adding that "first-quarter 1997 will still prove weak, with so far only demand for special steel wires and the new activities being firm".
It added that stocks in steel cord were at a low level, with demand not yet having picked up and industrial steel wires continuing to have a difficult time.
By 1330 GMT Bekaert was down 0.27 percent at 18,650 francs.
